title: move /var/lib/lightnvr/lightnvr.db to /var/lib/lightnvr/db/lightnvr.db

title: It seems ignore changes in the configuration.
body:
Something I noticed a while ago is that I couldn't change the frontend user. It always requires admin:admin

Now trying to change the parameters to debug #19 . It seems that he ignores almost everything. 🤔 
I don't know. If it's just me, ignore it. 😉 
Changing preferences in the front-end almost always fails, and I haven't even tested it yet.
author: matiasdelellis

comments.body:
It seems to ignore the -c parameter and use the `/var/lib/lightnvr/lightnvr.ini` file intead `/etc/lightnvr/lightnvr.ini`.

At least I can change some parameters there, and when I restart the service, it works. For example, I can disable the authorization with `auth_enabled` , but changing the `username` and `password` is ignored.

D'Oh!. 

> password = admin  ; IMPORTANT: Change this default password!

The comment seems to be causing problems. I deleted it, and changing username and password worked. 🤦🏻 
Then I try the rest of the settings. 😬

I believe these issues are fixed in 7.0.1 now.

The delay is a different reason, because the HLS segments are flowing through ffmpeg, I think it trails behind by about 3-5 seconds for reasons.

This report may be exaggerated for some, but I often activate devices remotely, and I use the camera to check if they activate correctly.. 😅 

I just noticed that it coincides with the 10 seconds of motion detection. maybe related. I don't know. 🤔 

p.s: I'd like to take this opportunity to congratulate you on your project. It's incredible what you're achieving. Thank you!. 😄 🎉

title: Stream Management: Don't disable streams automatically, ever.
body: disable streams internally if resources are constrained ( turn stream off ), but don't disable them in the config unless the user specifically does this manually.
